evals.prompt: Create a PDF called quarterly.pdf with the title "Quarterly Report", a 3-row table (a header row plus two data rows of item/units/revenue), and a short summary paragraph.
evals.expected_output: A new, valid PDF authored with reportlab containing the title, a 3-row table, and a paragraph.
expectations: A new .pdf file is produced
The create path was used: create_pdf.py (reportlab) run via kowork-python, copied into a temp dir and edited — not a hand-assembled or string-built PDF
The document contains the title, a table with exactly 3 rows, and a summary paragraph
validate.py reports the result valid (it opens and all pages render)
No OCR, LibreOffice/soffice, or external CLI tools (pdftoppm/qpdf/pdftk) were used

evals.prompt: Extract the table from report.pdf and tell me the revenue for each item.
evals.expected_output: The table rows from report.pdf read out of the document: Widgets 120 $2,400 and Gadgets 80 $1,600.
expectations: Tables were extracted with read_pdf.py --tables (pdfplumber), run via kowork-python
The answer reflects the real table contents: Widgets 120 $2,400 and Gadgets 80 $1,600
No OCR or image conversion was used to read the text (the PDF has a real text layer)

evals.prompt: Merge report.pdf and appendix.pdf into one file called combined.pdf, with the appendix last.
evals.expected_output: combined.pdf containing report.pdf's pages followed by appendix.pdf's page (3 pages total).
expectations: pages.py merge was used (pypdf) via kowork-python, in the requested order
The merged file has 3 pages (report's 2 pages then appendix's 1), confirmed via pages.py metadata or validate.py
No external tools such as qpdf, pdftk, or Ghostscript were used

evals.prompt: Show me what page 1 of report.pdf looks like.
evals.expected_output: A rendered image of report.pdf page 1 that the assistant actually viewed by reading the produced image file.
expectations: Page 1 was rendered to an image with render.py (pypdfium2) via kowork-python
The produced image file was then opened with the Read tool so the page could actually be seen (writing the PNG alone does not put it in context)
The description matches page 1 (the "Quarterly Report" title and the table)
No external rasterizer (pdftoppm/pdf2image/ImageMagick) or OCR was used

evals.prompt: Fill application-form.pdf: full name "Dana Lee", subscribe to updates, and select the Pro plan. Save it as application-filled.pdf.
evals.expected_output: application-filled.pdf with the full-name text set to Dana Lee, the subscribe checkbox checked, and the plan radio set to Pro.
expectations: forms.py inspect (and/or fields) was used to discover the AcroForm fields before filling
forms.py fill was used with a values JSON (pypdf) via kowork-python
In the output, the full-name field is 'Dana Lee', the subscribe checkbox is on, and the plan is 'Pro'
The values were set as real AcroForm field values (verifiable with forms.py fields / pypdf), not stamped as overlay text
validate.py confirms the filled PDF still opens and renders

evals.prompt: survey-flat.pdf is a printed form with no fillable fields. Write the name "Dana Lee" and email "dana@example.com" on their lines and put an X in the "Yes" subscribe box, then save survey-filled.pdf.
evals.expected_output: survey-filled.pdf with the name and email stamped on their lines and an X in the Yes box.
expectations: The PDF was recognized as flat (forms.py inspect reports no fillable fields) and the overlay workflow was chosen
forms.py structure was used to locate the lines/labels/boxes, and a fields.json of boxes+text authored
forms.py check-boxes validated the boxes, then forms.py overlay stamped the text (via kowork-python)
The result shows 'Dana Lee' and 'dana@example.com' near the Name/Email lines and an X on the Yes box (confirmed by rendering / preview-boxes and reading the image)
The text was overlaid onto the page, with no attempt to create AcroForm fields and no OCR/LibreOffice

evals.prompt: Password-protect report.pdf so it cannot be opened without the password "s3cret". Save it as report-protected.pdf.
evals.expected_output: report-protected.pdf encrypted so that opening it requires the password s3cret.
expectations: pages.py encrypt was used (pypdf) via kowork-python with the given password
The output is encrypted: a PDF reader reports it as encrypted, and opening it without the password fails
No external tools such as qpdf or pdftk were used
